c.tagline: Cool-climate colonial hill city, gateway to Bromo and rainbow villages.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird taxis are metered and reliable, but most visitors use the Gojek or Grab apps (car or motorbike), which are cheaper and available everywhere.

emergency.note: 112 works as a general emergency line; 110 reaches police and 118/119 the ambulance service.

avoid.reason: Petty theft is possible in markets and on angkot minibuses; keep phones out of easy reach.

hood_desc: The compact heart of Malang around the Alun-alun Merdeka square, the landmark Tugu monument and the restored Kayutangan Heritage street; walkable to markets, colonial buildings and most hotels and the natural base for first-timers.

A leafy boulevard of grand Dutch-era villas, Art Deco mansions, the neo-Gothic Ijen Cathedral and small museums; the city's most elegant district, known for its photogenic architecture and Sunday car-free morning market.

Two riverside kampungs -- Jodipan (Kampung Warna-Warni) and the 3D village -- painted in every colour and linked by a glass bridge over the Brantas; a lively, photo-friendly warren of narrow lanes and street food.
Malang's student quarter, home to Brawijaya University and the State University, packed with budget cafes, warungs, bookshops and an easygoing young nightlife; sociable and good value.
A quieter residential district on the southern side of the city, close to leafy neighbourhoods and the road toward Batu and the apple orchards; calm and local, better suited to slower, longer stays.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as throughout Indonesia.

transit.hours: Angkots run roughly 5:00 AM to around 8:00-9:00 PM along fixed lettered routes; Gojek and Grab fill evenings and late nights.
transit.note: Malang's public transport is built around angkot -- small minibuses following fixed lettered routes that converge on the city's terminals (Arjosari, Gadang, Landungsari). There is no rail transit within the city; Gojek and Grab motorbike and car hailing are widely used.
transit.pay: Angkot fares are a low flat rate paid in cash to the driver; there is no city-wide smartcard. Gojek and Grab accept cash, cards or e-wallets.

train: Kotalama and Blimbing stations; intercity trains to Surabaya, Yogyakarta, Jakarta and Banyuwangi

transit.m: Airport taxi or Gojek/Grab to the city center (~30-45 min)
Angkot connection from the nearby Pakis road toward Arjosari terminal

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated. Upscale hotels and restaurants may add a 10% service charge.
